conclusion.leading_causal_interpretation: deterministic row-dependent numerical behavior in batched CPU policy inference
conclusion.root_cause_localization: The first exact difference is localized to policy inference output; the probe alone does not identify a lower-level kernel or prove that rounding is the mechanism.
conclusion.successor_requirement: Evaluate every byte-distinct policy observation as a batch of one and broadcast its action to byte-identical lanes. Bind and sanitize GS_PARA_LEVEL=0 independently so the physics execution mode is explicit. Re-run a common-prefix-only exact lockstep probe before authorizing a successor smoke.

interpretive_basis: Both parallelization settings diverged after the first 20 ms policy step with exactly the same component, maximum absolute difference, RMS difference, and affected lanes.
Every captured physical component and the executed command remained bitwise equal; only the newly cached policy action differed.
At the first step, simulated action latency executes the common zero action history, so the physical equality is expected even though the newly inferred action is cached for the next step.
The installed RSL inference policy defaults to deterministic output and its Gaussian deterministic path returns the actor mean; the successor source also requests stochastic_output=false explicitly.
The probe does not demonstrate branch generation, RGB rendering, artifact completeness, training-set fitness, generalization, or any world-model result.
